user_problem: City bus routes bunch up so three buses arrive together then nothing for half an hour. Commuters want evenly spaced arrivals without adding buses.

mechanism_state.mechanism: Holding control — deliberately delaying buses at stops (or combining holding with other measures) so that buses on the same route do not travel closely together, thereby regularizing headways.
mechanism_state.intervention: Deploy an AVL/APC-driven holding scheme on the existing fleet: when a bus runs ahead of its predecessor's headway target, hold it at time-point stops (and combine with minor speed adjustment of the trailing bus) to enforce even spacing — no additional buses required.
mechanism_state.expected_effect: Evenly spaced arrivals and reduced bunching (fewer "three buses together, then nothing" events), lower headway variance, and shorter average commuter waiting time without fleet expansion.
